LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Melody. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify melodic sounds from the environment for aural discrimination, by animals and birds such as the
2. identify melodic variations in simple familiar tunes to enhance familiar tunes with variations in 316 Property of the Government of Kenya listening skills and as a basis for composition,
3. create simple melodic variations in familiar tunes as a basis for variations. composition and for enjoyment.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify melodic sounds from the environment for aural discrimination, by animals and birds such as the
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify melodic sounds from the environment for aural discrimination, by animals and birds such as the. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify melodic variations in simple familiar tunes to enhance familiar tunes with variations in 316 Property of the Government of Kenya listening skills and as a basis for composition,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify melodic variations in simple familiar tunes to enhance familiar tunes with variations in 316 Property of the Government of Kenya listening skills and as a basis for composition,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. create simple melodic variations in familiar tunes as a basis for variations. composition and for enjoyment.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to create simple melodic variations in familiar tunes as a basis for variations. composition and for enjoyment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Melody.
2. Explain Melody to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Melody.
4. Show that you can: identify melodic sounds from the environment for aural discrimination, by animals and birds such as the
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Melody. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Melody important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify melodic sounds from the environment for aural discrimination, by animals and birds such as the
2. identify melodic variations in simple familiar tunes to enhance familiar tunes with variations in 316 Property of the Government of Kenya listening skills and as a basis for composition,
3. create simple melodic variations in familiar tunes as a basis for variations. composition and for enjoyment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
